messages.author: e68f166a319176d9
messages.subject: Using R-INLA SPDE approach in large river system
parts:
Hello,
I am analyzing catch rate data from the Mississippi River using a zero-adjusted gamma model in R-INLA. I am able to run and validate the models but it has become apparent that there is a spatial component with catch rates in the southern part of the sampling area generally being higher than those in the northern part of the sampling area. Sampling was clustered in/near tributaries of the Mississippi such that the distance between sites is hugely variable (<1km - >400km). In an attempt to address the spatial component of this model, I used the SPDE approach with a nonconvex hull to create the mesh. This improved the model fit but correlations were not limited to the river. Because the study area is narrow relative to it's length, I have not been able to find a reasonable way to create a mesh that is suitable for this situation. I appreciate any insights or suggestions about how to address this problem.
Thanks,
Ben

parts:
Thank you for the reply and I apologize for the delayed response. I looked into the barrier model in more detail and, after working through various adjustments, I think I've come up with a mesh that will do what I want. Because I had to set the cutoff very low in this case (due to the width of the river), the mesh now has >50000 nodes. Having never dealt with a mesh of this size before, I'm uncertain what to expect in terms of computing time. Do you have any suggestion for further modifications to the mesh that will reduce the number of nodes or a means of tracking the progress of the model (e.g., % complete) so that I can anticipate how long it will take to run? I've included a few pieces of my code for reference. Any suggestions are appreciated.
Thanks,
Ben

max.edge <- 100000
MSR.bdry2 <- as.inla.mesh.segment(MSR_ShapeFile_UTM2)

mesh9.5 <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = MSR.bdry2,
                        max.edge = c(1, 2) * max.edge,
                        cutoff = 50)

river.tri <- inla.over_sp_mesh(MSR_ShapeFile_UTM2,
                               y = mesh9.5,
                               type = 'centroid',
                               ignore.CRS = T)

num.tri <- length(mesh9.5$graph$tv[, 1])
barrier.tri <- setdiff(1:num.tri, river.tri)

poly.barrier <- inla.barrier.polygon(mesh9.5,
                                     barrier.triangles = barrier.tri)

inla(...control.inla=list( int.strategy = "eb")...)

also

inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

also is your model a spatio-temporal model, if so reducing the temporal scale can greatly speed up the model,

cheers,
Sylvan

parts:
Hi all,
I was able to find a solution to this issue and decided to post it here in case someone else is running into a similar problem. Essentially, instead of using the inla mesh segment object as the boundary, I created a nonconvex hull and used that object as the interior argument in the inla.mesh.2d function (code below). Hopefully this is helpful to someone else down the line.
Ben

MSR.bdry2 <- as.inla.mesh.segment(MSR_ShapeFile_UTM2)

# create the hull
domain <- inla.nonconvex.hull(as.matrix(loc))

# I reset the max.edge argument
max.edge <- 50000

# create the mesh
mesh2 <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = domain,
                      interior = MSR.bdry2,
                      max.edge = max.edge,
                      cutoff = 50)

# define the projector matrix for the mesh
A2 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh2,
                       loc = as.matrix(loc))

# find the location of the centroids of all triangles in the mesh
NumTri <- length(mesh2$graph$tv[,1])
PosTri <- matrix(0, NumTri, 2)
for (t in 1:NumTri){
  Temp       <- mesh2$loc[mesh2$graph$tv[t, ], ]
  PosTri[t,] <- colMeans(Temp)[c(1,2)]
}


PosTri <- SpatialPoints(PosTri,
                        CRS("+proj=utm +zone=15 +datum=WGS84"))

# which triangles fall in the river
TriangleOutBarrier <- over(MSR_ShapeFile_UTM2, PosTri, returnList = T)
TriangleOutBarrier <- unlist(TriangleOutBarrier)

# find the triangles in the barrier (land)
TriangleInBarrier <- setdiff(1:NumTri, TriangleOutBarrier)

# create the barrier polygon and the spde object
BarrierPoly <- inla.barrier.polygon(mesh2, TriangleInBarrier)

Range0      <- 5000
AlphaRange0 <- 0.05
Sigma0      <- 2.5
AlphaSigma0 <- 0.05

spde2 <- inla.barrier.pcmatern(mesh2,
                               barrier.triangles = TriangleInBarrier,

prior.range = c(Range0, AlphaRange0),
                               prior.sigma = c(Sigma0, AlphaSigma0),
                               range.fraction = 0.1)
